title: fix(app-shell): the metadata form routes a condition builder to a member the served derivation marks as an erased string arm (objectui#9830)
body:
Fixes #9830
Clause-②: no

This is the ruling-B half of objectui#9830 (maintainer ruling `5749198339`, unlocked by triage `5903942724`). Deliverable ① landed as PR objectui#9911.

## What changed

`SchemaForm`'s shared shape test, `admitsString()`, now reads the declaration mark `x-objectstack-erased-authoring-input`. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 17.5.0 and later puts this mark on an arm whose authoring type a transform erased. A new module-private reader, `erasedAuthoringType()`, returns the erased type only for a well-formed version-1 mark.

- A mark that names `string` counts as a string arm, so a served predicate slot reaches `detectConditionWidget` and gets the condition builder.
- These still keep the veto: a mark that names another type, a mark of another version, a malformed mark, and an unmarked `{}`.
- No key name is read as evidence of a type, so ruling A stays refused.
- An explicit form-spec `widget` still decides outright, because `resolveFieldWidget` runs no detector when one is set.

## The reading the triage asked for

The instrument was the published packages, installed fresh from npm into an isolated scratch directory: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol@17.5.0`, `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0`, and `zod@4.6.5`, the zod peer objectui's lockfile resolves spec 17.5.0 with. I called the projection method that the `/meta/types` route calls, `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.getMetaTypes()`. Its stub engine registry listed the 30 schema-bearing types (`listMetadataTypeSchemaTypes()` plus `listUnregisteredKindSchemaTypes()`), and the result was JSON round-tripped the way the wire carries it. I did not boot a backend, so this is the projection's output, not an HTTP response.

| node | served bytes |
|:--|:--|
| SUBJECT `hook.condition.anyOf[0]` | `{"x-objectstack-erased-authoring-input":{"version":1,"type":"string"}}` |
| `hook.condition` itself, and its envelope arm `anyOf[1]` | no mark |
| IN-PAYLOAD CONTROL `hook.condition.anyOf[1].properties.ast` | `{}`, no mark |
| OPEN MEMBER `field.defaultValue` | a `description` only, no mark (the same for `flow.variables.items.defaultValue`) |
| RETRY-ARM TYPE `action.visible` | no mark (it is served from the `io: 'input'` retry, where nothing is erased) |

⇒ The mark sits on the erased arm itself, inside the member's `anyOf`. It is not on the member's own schema and not on the envelope. `admitsString()` already visits every arm, so it reads the mark on each node it visits, the same place it reads `type`.

Across the whole served document, the mark appears 80 times: 50 name `string`, 25 name `object` and 5 name `array`. Because some marks name other types, the reader checks the mark's `type` and does not treat its presence alone as a string arm.

## Dispatch item 4: do the other four detectors move?

I checked every property member of the 30 served entries (4021 members). The five detectors were copied verbatim, and the field-ref detector was given a wired catalog, which is the worst case.

| | members |
|:--|--:|
| `admitsString` changes (every one from false to true) | 50 |
| … and the resolved widget changes, every one from unset to `condition` | 45 |
| … and the widget changes for field-ref, secret, icon or colour | **0** |
| … and no detector claims the name (`field.expression`, `object.fields.*.expression`, `object.titleFormat`, `job.schedule.expression`, one `when` under `object`'s `$defs`) | 5 |

So the mark read stays in `admitsString()` rather than being scoped to the condition detector. The mark is shape information, and one schema should not get two answers to "does this admit a string?", which is the split PR objectui#9911 removed. On today's served surface, the read changes nothing outside the condition route.

## Before and after on the real served entries

This was a one-off render, not committed. I passed the verbatim 17.5.0 `hook`, `field` and `sharing_rule` entries (schema plus served form, with the collapsed sections opened) through the real `SchemaForm`, with `conditionScope: 'flattened'`. The base column is the same probe run inside ablation leg 1 below.

| served member | without the mark read (base) | this branch |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `hook.condition` (form row `type: 'code'`, `language: 'expression'`) | code editor | condition builder |
| `field.visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` (same form-row shape) | code editor | condition builder |
| `sharing_rule.condition` (no served form) | plain text area | condition builder |
| control `field.defaultValue` (open member) | text area | text area |
| control `hook.name` (plain string) | input | input |

## Pins

- **New file, `SchemaForm.erasedArmMark-9830.test.tsx`.** One render holds all of these:
  - the verbatim served `hook.condition` as the MARKED subject, which gets the builder;
  - the UNMARKED husk as the control, which gets no builder;
  - an arm with an `object` mark, which gets no builder;
  - an arm with a version-2 mark, which gets no builder;
  - a marked arm under the name `expression`, which gets no builder because the name still chooses;
  - a whole-render accounting check, where exactly one field mounts.

  A second render uses a form spec to check both directions of precedence. On an unmarked husk, an authored `widget: 'condition'` mounts the builder, which is the door the ruling named for authors. On a marked husk, an authored `widget: 'textarea'` is kept.
- **Existing file, `SchemaForm.nestedAnyOfPredicate-9830.test.tsx`.** The husk-boundary case keeps its assertion unchanged. It is now named the UNMARKED husk, and its header points to the sibling file for the inversion.

## Ablations

The fix was committed first as `630c6838f`. Each leg was written with `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, and each restore was proven by the blob matching HEAD and by an empty `git diff HEAD`.

1. **Delete the mark read.** The anchor was `if (erasedAuthoringType(branch)?.includes('string')) return true;`, which went from 1 hit to 0; the blob went from `8db9c224` to `2cddb54e`. Result: **3 failed / 12 passed**. The failures were the marked-subject case, the same-render control case (it also asserts the subject's builder), and the accounting case. The served probe in the same run produced the base column above. Restored to `8db9c224`.
2. **Read the mark's presence instead of its value.** The replacement was `if (branch[ERASED_AUTHORING_INPUT_KEYWORD]) return true;`; the blob went from `8db9c224` to `cc83a6d6`. Result: **2 failed / 10 passed**. The failures were the value case (the `object` mark and the version-2 mark) and the accounting case, while the subject stayed green. Restored to `8db9c224`.

I did not re-run the third direction, reading a bare `{}` as a string arm. The existing file's unmarked-husk assertion is unchanged, and PR objectui#9911's ablation 2 proved it can go red.

No `dist` is involved: both pins import `./SchemaForm` from `src`.

## Gates

- Tests: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` at `630c6838f` passed **352 of 352 files**, with 4194 tests passed and 1 skipped (lock verdict: command-exit 0). The two pins alone: 12 of 12 passed.
- Type-check: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exited 0. The closure was built first with `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`, which also exited 0. The package's `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`, so the pins are compiled.
- Lint: `pnpm exec eslint` on the three changed source and test files exited 0, with 0 errors. It gave 16 warnings, all pre-existing in `SchemaForm.tsx` and none on a changed hunk; the two test files had none.
- On the final head `5355be25c`, every one of these exited 0:
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
  - `check:control-bytes`
  - `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations)
  - `check:changeset-claims`
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`
  - `check:test-path-roots`
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`
  - `check-changeset-no-major`
  - `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the 4 paths, which answered **NOT GOVERNED**
- `5355be25c` differs from `630c6838f` only in the prose of `.changeset/9830-erased-arm-mark.md`, so the test, type-check and lint runs above measured this head's code.
- **NOT MEASURED, declared to CI:** the rest of the `packages/app-shell` tests, the `apps/console` tests, and the repo-wide `pnpm lint`. The narrowing is proven: behaviour changes only for a schema that carries the keyword, and `git grep` for the keyword over the whole base tree `0ffc423b1` found 0 hits (exit 1). The control in the same family, `admitsString` in `SchemaForm.tsx` at base, found 7 hits. So no fixture outside the two pins can change its verdict.

## Acceptance notes

- **The face changes on served form rows declared with `type: 'code'`.** `hook.condition` and `field.visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` are served with `type: 'code', language: 'expression'`. That is a field type, not a `widget`, so under the precedence already written in `admitsString()`'s header the condition detector now selects the builder over the code editor. This is the outcome the ruling asked for: the generic-form arm of objectui#8167 becomes reachable. If a producer wants the code editor on such a row, its form spec pins `widget: 'code'`. Noted, not filed; carrier: none.
- **The pending changeset from PR objectui#9911 is now narrower than it reads.** That changeset, `9830-nested-anyof-predicate-string-arm.md`, is not yet released, and it says the husk gets no builder. This PR's changeset narrows that statement in its own words: it now holds for an UNMARKED husk only. I did not edit the older file, because it is outside this claim's file surface. If the seat prefers the older body corrected in place, the change is one sentence in its last paragraph.
- **The reader accepts only version 1 of the mark.** If objectstack bumps the mark's version, the builder quietly returns to the veto, which is the pre-mark behaviour, until objectui's reader follows. That is the conservative direction, chosen on purpose.
- **objectui spells the keyword once, as `ERASED_AUTHORING_INPUT_KEYWORD`.** `@objectstack/spec` does not export it, and the emitter lives in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, which objectui does not depend on.
